messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH - hosted-inference-503s (policy: prod-critical) triggered 03:41:00 UTC. Primary oncall @jamie did not acknowledge within 90s, escalating.
jamie: ugh phone on low battery, just saw pings. what's the symptom?
priya: dashboards show 5xx spike across eu-central-1 and us-west-2, started ~03:40 UTC. overall 5xx ~28%, peak 52% on some frontends.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation: alert routed to secondary (samir) 1a Please acknowledge within 2m.
samir: acknowledged. on it. can someone paste last 30s of proxy logs and any recent infra changes?
oncall-sre: quick tail from model-router logs:
```
2026-03-16T03:40:22Z warn connection reset by peer
2026-03-16T03:40:26Z error upstream unavailable
2026-03-16T03:40:30Z info endpointslice update: count=18 delta=+12
```
oncall-sre: looks like a burst of endpoint updates correlated with the start time.
jamie: was there an infra job running? infra-tooling had a scheduled endpoint sync at 03:39 as part of a group resync.
infra-tooling-bot: auto-resync job #453 triggered at 03:39:10 UTC for controller resync.
priya: customer impact: search-suggestions and chat-suggest are the most affected. CS reporting a handful of escalations from mid-market clients. not full outage but user-facing errors and retries.
manager-luis: paging me due to manager-escalation (primary missed ack). I'm awake and on call. what's the plan?
samir: initial mitigation: 1) pause infra resync job (jamie), 2) mark flapping endpoints as draining, 3) shift 50% traffic to healthy pool-c, 4) enable short circuit-breaker to return 429 vs 503 where appropriate.
jamie: paused job via infra-tooling: `infra-tooling pause 453` - confirmed, queue cleared.
oncall-sre: removed 4 flapping pods from service endpoints. controller backoff observed.
samir: routing change applied: 50% -> pool-c; routers show successful rehoming.
priya: logs after change show 5xx down from 28% -> 9% in 60s. customer error reports slowing.
cs-rep: will draft a CS message: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors between 03:40-03:46 UTC in some regions; mitigation applied and service restored. Please reach out to support@redwood.ai if you saw persistent issues." ok to send?
manager-luis: hold until we confirm stable for 10m; then send. also add contact for urgent escalations.
jamie: small but important note: my DND blocked the initial page; need to remind team to have backup contact if primary unreachable.
priya: adding: observed TCP resets between router and model-proxy on SNI mismatch in a subset of pods - adding to timeline.
samir: applied circuit-breaker config on router: `max_attempts=3 backoff=200ms fallback=429` to reduce 503 amplification.
oncall-sre: metrics: 5xx at 3% now, tail latency improving; still watching for endpoint oscillation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: manager escalation triggered - notifying manager-luis due to primary missed ack.
manager-luis: acknowledged manager escalation. assigning post-incident owner: jamie to draft postmortem if customer-impacting > 10m.
jamie: will own postmortem. immediate followups: 1) add rate-limit to controller resyncs, 2) improve endpoint-change jitter, 3) add health-check backoff in model-proxy. assigning to infra and runtime teams.
cs-rep: heads-up: one customer ticket looks like it persisted longer (search-suggestions client). I'll include specific request IDs and ask for followup from eng.
samir: leaving runbook notes in the incident doc and adding router flags used.
priya: quick check: any deploys around window? none in model-proxy or router since 01:00 UTC. root cause likely controller resync + endpoint churn.
oncall-sre: also noted kube-apiserver latency spike at 03:39:09 which amplified the update flood; adding to timeline.
jamie: handing over to day-shift in 45m. thanks for quick responses.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by samir at 03:42:15 UTC.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert resolved at 03:46:05 UTC after manual mitigation and routing changes. auto-close checklist queued.
manager-luis: good work. jamie, please include timeline, root cause, and action items in postmortem. if CS needs a customer-facing blurb earlier, we can approve a short message.
samir: leaving my ack, tidying router changes to ensure no config drift.
cs-rep: will prepare targeted messages for affected customers and flag any requests for SLA credits.
jamie: closing thread here, will open postmortem doc and ping owners. thanks team :thumbsup:
